Every hex encoding in the claim's evidence_disasm string matches my independent re-disassembly byte-for-byte.

Confirmed mov r0,#0xac (0x02157148) / bl 0x201a21c (0x02157150) / mov sl,r0 (0x02157154): a fresh, independent 172-byte heap allocation with no relationship to r8 or the 0x02053528 constructor. This is a genuinely distinct object; the offset overlap with the character struct's +0x98-0xa1 is coincidental as claimed.

Confirmed ldr r0,[r5,#0xc] (0x02081148) then add r8,r0,#0xa4 (0x02081160); scanned all r8-touching instructions across the full 2868-byte function body and r8 is never reassigned again before the flagged accesses. strhhi r1,[r8,#0xa8] / strhhi r2,[r8,#0xaa] (0x0208162C/0x02081630) and str r0,[r8,#0xb0] (0x02081584) therefore land at entity+0x14c/+0x14e/+0x154 (0xa4+0xa8, 0xa4+0xaa, 0xa4+0xb0), not the character struct's own +0xa8/+0xaa/+0xb0. This is a correctly-identified base-provenance aliasing false lead.

0x02158E78-0x02158E84 disassembles to exactly ldrsb r0,[sl,#0xe0]; cmp r0,#0; subne r0,r0,#1; strbne r0,[sl,#0xe0] -- the NE-predicated pair only fires when the loaded byte is nonzero, so the value stays at 0 once it hits the floor and otherwise decrements by 1: a textbook decrement-with-floor-at-zero in 4 instructions, byte-identical to the quoted evidence.

0x0207D16C is confirmed a true leaf (callees=0): strh r1,[r0,#0xa0] (16-bit store) followed by ldr r1,[r0,#0x78]/orr r1,r1,#0x800000/str r1,[r0,#0x78] (32-bit read-modify-write). Note 0x800000 is bit23 (byte 2 of the word), not the low byte holding the 0x00/0x22/0xc0 enum -- but the claim is careful to say only 'the SAME 4-byte-aligned word', not the same byte, so this is accurately described, not overstated. Call site 0x020858EC-F4 confirmed as r1=ldrsh[r8,#0x1a], r0=ldr[r6,#0x10], bl 0x207d16c; r6 is confirmed reloaded from an array via an r5-indexed load (ldr r6,[r0,r5,lsl#2] at 0x02085878) inside caller 0x02085704, consistent with the claimed per-entry-loop rebinding. The claim is correctly flagged SPECULATIVE and the code matches its own hedged description; identity of [r6+0x10] is genuinely unresolved statically, as stated.
